papers.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

papers.title: Generic properties of the Laplace spectrum and eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: We prove that the spectrum of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary is generically linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we prove that pointwise products of eigenfunctions generically are linearly independent. The proof is based on conformal perturbations of the metric. The result implies in particular that generically the truncation of the continuous functions on $M$ by spectral projections of the Laplace operator is given by symmetric matrices.

papers.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
papers.abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

papers.title: Isometric Embeddings of Asymptotically Hyperbolic Manifolds into Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: The Nash Embedding theorem asserts that every closed Riemannian manifold can be isometrically embedded into a Euclidean space of sufficiently high dimension. In this paper, we address the asymptotically hyperbolic version of the problem. We prove that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $\left(M,g\right)$ can be realized as a submanifold of a sufficiently high-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathrm{H}^{N+1}$, intersecting the sphere at infinity transversely, if and only if $g$ is asymptotically Poincar\'e-Einstein to second order.

papers.title: Steady conformally K\"{a}hler Ricci solitons with isoparametric potential
papers.abstract: We classify complete, non-compact, simply connected, irreducible four-dimensional steady gradient Ricci solitons that are globally conformally K\"ahler and have an isoparametric potential. The steady Ricci solitons are $U(2)$-invariant nuts on $\mathbb R^4$, including the Bryant and Cao solitons, and bolts on $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb R^2$ and on $\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathbb{CP}^1$. For each $m\ge3$ there is exactly one non-collapsed bolt. A key step, valid for Ricci solitons of every sign, is that away from the locally conformally flat case, the conformal factor is aligned with the potential function, which yields cohomogeneity-one symmetry.

papers.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period. In this paper we will show that the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow is free. We use symplectic geometry to investigate the topology of the quotient of the unit tangent bundle T^1M/S^1 by the S^1 action that comes from the geodesic flow. We show that this quotient admits the structure of a smooth symplectic manifold and that this symplectic manifold is symplectomorphic to S^2 \times S^2 equipped with a split form. This will enable a computation involving the Euler class of the orbibundle T^1M\rightarrow T^1M/S^1 which will lead to a solution of Berger's conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds.

papers.title: Conformal geodesics and gauged Killing-Yano forms in dimension four
papers.abstract: We study the relation between conformal geodesics and conformal Killing-Yano (CKY) 2-forms on anti-self-dual conformal manifolds of dimension 4. In the flat case, twistor quadrics determine self-dual CKY forms whose zero loci contain conformal geodesics. To extend this construction to curved manifolds, we consider self-dual 2-forms with values in a line bundle and satisfying the gauged CKY equation, coupled to connections with anti-self-dual curvature. In this way we provide a local ambient characterization of non-null conformal geodesics as zero curves of gauged CKY forms, with the curvature vanishing along these curves.

papers.title: Rigidity in sharp eigenvalue estimates for differential forms
papers.abstract: For $1\leq p\leq n/2$, we derive sharp eigenvalue estimates for the Hodge Laplacian on differential $p$-forms under the curvature condition introduced by Petersen and Wink, and study their equality cases. Equality recovers the stronger curvature operator lower bound and, in the closed case, leaves only round or Sasakian metrics on the universal cover. For manifolds with boundary, weak $p$-convexity of the boundary makes the unit hemisphere the only equality case for the absolute boundary problem.

papers.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (II): strong uniqueness
papers.abstract: We prove strong uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of a closed Ricci flow when one tangent flow is generated by a complete smooth asymptotically conical Ricci shrinker. The modified flow converges to this shrinker in a fixed gauge, with quantitative estimates on expanding domains. The main ingredients are a {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon inequality for Perelman's entropy, based on the global weighted divergence-free gauge constructed in the preceding paper, and estimates controlling the geometric radius under Ricci flow.

papers.title: The regular set of Ricci limit spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X,d,p)$ be a nontrivial pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit of complete connected Riemannian $n$-manifolds satisfying $\operatorname{Ric}\geq-(n-1)g$. For $1\leq j\leq n$, set \[ \mathcal{R}_j(X) = \bigl\{x\in X:\text{ every tangent cone at } x \text{ is isometric to } \mathbb{R}^j\bigr\}, \qquad \mathcal{R}(X)=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^n\mathcal{R}_j(X). \] We prove that there is a unique $k$ such that $\mathcal{R}(X)=\mathcal{R}_k(X)$, answering the pointwise regular-dimension question originating in Cheeger and Colding's work~\cite[p408]{CC97}. We construct a volume-corrected heat entropy on RCD space and identify the distributional logarithmic-density defect $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Hess} f)-\Delta f$ by Green-volume regularization.

papers.title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

papers.title: On the Geroch conjecture for toric gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: Geroch conjectured that the local solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with two commuting Killing fields and vanishing twist constants are generated from flat space by an infinite-dimensional group of transformations, and Hauser and Ernst proved this for stationary axisymmetric spacetimes near the axis. The solutions generated from flat space by the transformations with finitely many poles in the spectral parameter are the solitons of Belinski and Zakharov. We prove a solitonic form of the conjecture in Riemannian signature, for toric gravitational instantons. The proof combines Weinstein's uniqueness argument, a closed formula for the soliton metrics in Hankel determinants and a degree argument. It also applies to the toric Ricci-flat metrics with conical singularities constructed by Li and Sun.

papers.title: Mean curvature bounds for CMC foliations of manifolds with sectional curvature bounded below
papers.abstract: Let $M^{n+1}$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\sec_M\ge-K_0$, $K_0\ge0$, and let $\mathfrak{F}$ be a codimension one foliation of $M$ by hypersurfaces of constant mean curvature, the constant depending on the leaf. We prove that the mean curvature of every leaf satisfies $|H|\le(n+1)\sqrt{K_0}$. In particular, the mean curvature of the leaves of a CMC foliation of a complete manifold with $|\sec_M|\le1$ is bounded by $n+1$, which answers positively a conjecture of Meeks III, P\'erez, and Ros.

papers.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.

papers.title: Holonomies of hyperbolic surfaces with one branch point
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. We prove that any representation of $\pi_1(S)$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ with Euler class $3-2g$ is the holonomy of a hyperbolic metric on $S$ with one simple branch point.

papers.title: A Riemannian approach for PDE-constrained shape optimization over the diffeomorphism group using outer metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the use of outer metrics, in particular Sobolev-type metrics on the diffeomorphism group in the context of PDE-constrained shape optimization. Leveraging the structure of the diffeomorphism group we analyze the connection between the push-forward of a smooth function defined on the diffeomorphism group and the classical shape derivative as an Eulerian semi-derivative. We consider in particular, two predominant examples on PDE-constrained shape optimization. An electric impedance tomography inspired problem, and the optimization of a two-dimensional bridge. These problems are numerically solved using the Riemannian steepest descent method where the descent directions are taken to be the Riemannian gradients associated to various outer metrics. For comparison reasons, we also solve the problem using other previously proposed Riemannian metrics in particular the Steklov-Poincar\'e metric.

papers.title: Sharp Sobolev inequalities on noncompact Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: Given a smooth, complete Riemannian manifold $M$ with bounded Ricci curvature and positive injectivity radius, we derive a sharp Sobolev inequality for the embedding of $W^{1,p}(M)$ into $L^{\frac{np}{n-p}}(M)$, when $1\le p< n$. We will first reduce the inequality to functions having support with small enough volume. In turn, we will show that the inequality for small volumes is implied by a first order uniform asymptotic expansion of the isoperimetric profile for $M$, for small volumes. We will then show that such an expansion follows from a local, uniform Sobolev inequality for functions in $W^{1,1}$, having support with small enough diameter.

papers.title: Sharp Sobolev and Moser-Trudinger inequalities on noncompact Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below
papers.abstract: We establish Sobolev and Moser-Trudinger inequalities with best constants on noncompact Riemannan manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below, and positive injectivity radius.

papers.title: Critical $p$-Laplace equations with monotone coefficients: Liouville classification and a Schoen-type Harnack inequality
papers.abstract: We investigate positive weak solutions of the critical $p$-Laplace equation $$ -\Delta_p u = u^{p^*-1} h(u), \qquad 1 < p < n, $$ where $h$ is a positive, bounded, continuous, and nonincreasing function. Our first main result is a complete classification of normalized, bounded, positive entire solutions for every equation in a compact family determined by $h$: Any such solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. Moreover, the existence of an Aubin--Talenti profile as a solution implies that $h$ is constant on the entire interval of values attained by that profile. Subsequently, applying this classification result, we establish the following scale-invariant Schoen-type estimate $$ \left(\sup_{B_R} u\right)\left(\inf_{B_{2R}} u\right)^{p-1} \le C R^{p-n} $$ for nonnegative weak solutions defined in $B_{3R}$. As a direct corollary, we apply the profound result of Ciraolo--Gatti \cite{CG2026} to obtain a fully unrestricted Liouville theorem: Every positive entire solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. For the purely critical equation, we also show that the corresponding Liouville classification is equivalent to a Schoen-type Harnack inequality. The arguments in this work give quasilinear versions of the Kelvin transform and the method of moving spheres, which was previously available only in the semilinear setting, and also yield alternative proofs of the classical results. The technique developed here can likely be extended to a wider class of Liouville-type problems for critical equations.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.title: The gauge fixing theorem with applications to the Yang-Mills flow over Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In 1982, Uhlenbeck \cite {U2} established the well-known gauge fixing theorem, which has played a fundamental role for Yang-Mills theory. In this paper, we apply the idea of Uhlenbeck to establish a parabolic type of gauge fixing theorems for the Yang-Mills flow and prove existence of a weak solution of the Yang-Mills flow on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold with initial value $A_0$ in $W^{1,n/2}(M)$. When $n=4$, we improve a key lemma of Uhlenbeck (Lemma 2.7 of \cite {U2}) to prove uniqueness of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow on a four dimensional manifold.

papers.title: Curved $\infty$-Local Systems And Projectively Flat Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
papers.abstract: We generalize the higher Riemann-Hilbert correspondence in the presence of scalar curvature for a (possibly non-compact) smooth manifold $M$. We show that the dg-category of curved $\infty$-local systems, the dg-category of graded vector bundles with projectively flat $\mathbb Z$-graded connections and the dg-category of curved representations of the singular simplicial set of the based loop space of $M$ are all $A_\infty$-quasi equivalent. They provide dg-enhancements of the subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant and have finite-dimensional fibers. In the ungraded case, we reduce to an equivalence between projectively flat vector bundles and a subcategory of projective representations of $\pi_1(M; x_0)$. As an application of our general framework, we also prove that the category of cohesive modules over the curved Dolbeault algebra of a complex manifold $X$ is equivalent to a subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules which generalizes a theorem due to Block to possibly non-compact complex manifolds.

papers.title: Critical metrics for the quadratic curvature functional on complete four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete four-dimensional Riemannian metrics on connected manifolds that are critical for the curvature functional $\A(g)=\int_M|\Rm|^2\,\vol$ and have finite curvature energy. If $\langle\Ract\E,\E\rangle\ge0$, where $\E=\Ric-\frac14\Scal\,g$ and $\Ract$ is the curvature action on symmetric two-tensors, then the metric is either Einstein or locally isometric to a product of surfaces of constant Gaussian curvatures $c$ and $-c$, with $c\ne0$. This extends the corresponding compact classification to the complete setting with finite curvature energy.

papers.title: Canonical parameters on marginally trapped surfaces in the Minkowski 4-space
papers.abstract: Marginally trapped surfaces are spacelike surfaces in the Minkowski space whose mean curvature vector is lightlike at each point. In general, the marginally trapped surfaces are determined by seven functions satisfying several conditions (differential equations). In the present paper, we introduce special principal parameters, called canonical, and prove that every marginally trapped surface of general type admits (at least locally) canonical principal parameters which allow us to reduce the number of functions. We prove a Fundamental existence and uniqueness theorem formulated in terms of canonical parameters, which states that every marginally trapped surface of general type is determined up to a motion by three smooth functions satisfying a system of partial differential equations. The special subclass of marginally trapped surfaces with parallel mean curvature vector field is described in terms of only one differential equation. Finally, the theory is enriched with examples of marginally trapped surfaces for which canonical parameters are determined.

papers.title: Topology of isometric classes and flows of geometric structures
papers.abstract: We study the topology of isometric classes of tensorial $H$-structures for closed and connected subgroups $H\leqslant\mathrm{SO}(n)$. The map assigning an $H$-structure its induced metric admits a global trivialization; consequently, the space of $H$-structures is homotopy equivalent to any fixed isometric class. On flat tori, these classes are mapping spaces into $\mathrm{SO}(n)/H$. We give examples with infinitely many connected components for $\mathrm{G}_2$, $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$, and almost Hermitian structures, determine the number of components for $\mathrm{SU}(m)$-structures on flat tori, and study the corresponding moduli spaces. For closed manifolds of dimension $n>2$, the intrinsic torsion energy on the full space of $H$-structures has infimum zero on every nonempty path component, and its critical points are precisely the torsion-free structures. In fixed isometric classes, we contrast the concentration phenomena underlying finite-time singularities with cohomological classes admitting positive energy lower bounds and harmonic representatives. Finally, we establish a lifting principle for metric-dependent flows, derive an evolution identity for isometric flows, and extend harmonic-flow estimates to general $H$-structures.

papers.title: Diffeological Riemannian orbifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the data of a Riemannian metric on a differentiable stack presented by an orbifold groupoid is equivalent to the data of a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space. As a consequence, we conclude that the classical notion of Riemannian orbifold is equivalent to that of a Riemannian diffeological orbifold. We use the framework for Riemannian diffeology introduced by Kuribayashi, Sakai, and Shiobara, and our result answers a problem they posed in the affirmative. More generally, we show that a Riemannian metric on a Lie groupoid, namely a 2-metric in the sense of del Hoyo and Fernandes, induces a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space only if the Lie groupoid is regular, and that properness is a sufficient but not necessary condition.

papers.title: Generalized Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence and Weil-Petersson current
papers.abstract: In this paper we extend Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence along holomorphic fibre space and we show that there exists a generalized Hermitian-Einstein metric which is twisted with Weil-Petersson current.In fact we generalise Song-Tian program for vector bundles

papers.title: Affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides
papers.abstract: We study affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides. An opposite-side involution sends a pencil through an interior point to a piecewise smooth family of lines. Its completed envelope consists of conic arcs and transition segments. The completed transform has non-positive oriented area. Maximising the negative oriented area and dividing by the polygonal area gives an affine invariant that vanishes precisely for centrally symmetric polygons. Combining an identity for reflected chord vectors with the Rogers--Shephard inequality shows that this invariant is strictly less than $1$, with optimal universal constant $1$. The energy extends continuously to the boundary and vanishes there. We also compare chord counts under compatible smoothing and prove Hausdorff convergence to the smooth transform.
